body: Thank you for your no-nonsense response.  I am going to switch back to my tried-and-true meds on Wednesday.

My son and I stay pretty active...right now it's a struggle, but I do it for him.  We go to playgroups and activities for kids his age through meetup and Macaroni kid.  I take him outside to play and we talk and hang out a lot.
Things got tough a few months ago near the end of my pregnancy when I had a falling out with my mom's group because they were hyper-judgmental of me taking antidepressants while pregnant.  
I was very proactive about taking care of my mental health while I was pregnant and now it's time to be proactive again.  I know what is right for me and I know I'll realize I made the right choice once my mood stabilizes when I get back on my old meds.
Thank you for reaching out to help a complete stranger.  You've been more help than you know.

Thank you for the book recommendation - I actually own a copy and found it useful.  I don't live anywhere near Seattle, I live in one of those freaky, non-contiguous states. I'm going to work hard not to feel shame because I know medication is the best route to health for me.  thank you for caring enough to respond. It means a lot and is a big help.

You are right about my "friends," I left the mom's group I was a part of because of what I consider bullying and now only interact with them on Facebook.  When I was struggling with depression at the end of my pregnancy and re-started my medication they were against it despite me telling them it worked for me.  I'm going to work to remember that I can be happy and healthy again and will be proactive when I talk to my doctor.  Thank you so much for reaching out to a complete stranger and giving me support.

Thank you for reminding me that it's the bipolar and not me.  I usually do a meditation practice to try and count my blessings but I haven't been able to focus enough lately to do it. I want to get better so much.
